name: Loki
whyHere: There is Precursor work in the Valley that nobody there understands, and you understand it, and that is dangerous for everyone including you.

deeds.description: Spoke a true thing in the shape the Unlit could hear — and the elder of the Deep acknowledged it.

chronicle: Loki read the four spike entries with Tessvel Cairn in the Pressure-Routing Annex, named the pattern — something moves deeper into the lower routing channel with each morning pass — and proposed both channel access and a more personal arrangement; Tessvel confirmed the access, asked for time on the rest, and left Loki knowing exactly where to find them.

Loki stood on the shelf above the terminus regulator and asked Cy for one honest reason to descend — Cy gave exactly one: three missing entries in its inventory of this installation class, records written into the stone below that no system above holds. The visit to the Unlit Deep reached its full close: Sable found and left in peace, the elder's deed named, the passage open, the regulator identified. What Loki carries out, and whether to return for the missing records, is the remaining thread.

turns.player: Descend again — take Cy to the inspection port and recover the three missing entries
turns.summary: Loki descended to the inspection port below the Unlit's outer chamber and recovered the three missing entries — the terminus regulator's calibration, its last full service record, and the condition of its failsafe.
turns.narration:
The passage smells of cold stone and something living — not rot, not decay, just the deep-water patience of a place that has been wet for a very long time. You descend with one hand trailing the left wall, where Prism Sight told you the creatures walk. Cy follows at your heel, its lamp held low so the light pools downward rather than outward. The Unlit above say nothing as you go. You do not look back to confirm the Standing Unlit is still there. You know they are.

The stair is not long, but it earns its depth. The worked stone changes character about halfway down — older cut, tighter joints, no sign of the Unlit's hand. This is the older floor. Cy's lens irises three times in quick succession when its feet touch the lower stones, and it does not close again. It recognizes the construction. It does not say so out loud, but the lens says it plainly enough.

The inspection port is not hidden. It sits in a recessed niche in the east wall, low enough that you have to crouch, sealed with a stone face that has a hand-worn depression in it — not a lock, a grip. You press your palm flat. The stone swings inward on a counterweight that has not corroded in the centuries since it was set. Behind it: three panels of worked metal, each stamped with a glyph you have seen on Cy's own housing. Line entries, precise and small. Cy steps forward, leans its lens within a finger's width of the first panel, and goes very still. After a moment it says, in its most careful voice, 'These were not in my inventory. They are in my inventory now.'

You do not rush it. The deep water sound is everywhere down here — not a stream, not a drip, but a continuous presence below the floor, as though the stone is floating on something patient and enormous. The three entries, you learn in pieces as Cy reads them aloud with the precise cadence of a thing reciting to itself: the regulator below this junction was calibrated to hold a temperature ceiling for the lines above; its last full service was recorded here, not in any system the valley holds; and its failsafe — the condition under which it would begin to wind down without external instruction — is a sustained drop in the watershed pressure it was built to monitor. The regulator is doing exactly what it was made to do. It has been doing it, alone, for a very long time.

*✦ The Thread of He Doesn'T Know, But He'S A Construct From The Time Before The Transition. His Parents Were Extremely Wealthy But They Were Always Traveling And Enjoying Their Nanite Powers. — a step forward.*

turns.player: Read the metal panels yourself with See the Made Thing — find what Cy's literal reading might miss
turns.summary: Loki read the installation panels with See the Made Thing and found what Cy's literal scan missed: the regulator was built for a named recipient to find — a personal designation stamped into the address glyph of the first panel.
turns.narration:
You hold the first panel flat against your palm and let See the Made Thing open. Not Cy's way of reading — the glyph-by-glyph inventory scan, methodical and complete. Your way: the whole thing at once, seams and all.

The panels are not a record in the ordinary sense. They are a conversation. The first calibration entry was stamped by someone who disagreed with the specification and said so in the margin — a single struck glyph that means something like 'this will hold but not forever.' The service record is signed twice, by two different hands, and the second signature is slightly larger, slightly more deliberate, the way a person signs when they are overruling someone. The failsafe entry is last. It reads: sustained drop in watershed pressure, below a threshold that is written right there in the metal, triggers autonomous wind-down. Full wind-down takes between one and two weeks. The regulator does not alert. It simply stops.

Then you see the thing Cy would not have named. All three panels are addressed. Not to a system, not to a maintenance log. The installation stamp at the top of the first panel carries a recipient glyph — an individual designation, personal, the kind used for a named assignment rather than a facility. Cy's lens has been reading the content. You read the shape. Someone built this for someone specific to find.

Cy tilts its lens up from the third panel and toward your face. It does not ask what you found. It waits. The deep water sound moves below the floor, patient and unhurried, and the open port niche is quiet around you both.

turns.player: Prism Sight the panels — look for heat-traces, older handling, any sign of who touched them last and when
turns.summary: Prism Sight revealed three sets of heat-traces on the installation panels — someone came here before Loki, read partially, and pressed a finger to the personal name on the third panel as though they recognized it.
turns.narration:
You close your eyes for a breath, then open them differently — Prism Sight settling into place the way a lens focuses, the world going from seen to read.

The first panel carries heat from your own hands now, fresh and recent. But beneath that, faint and cooling fast, three older traces. Whoever last held this panel before you held it a long time — the warmth is evenly distributed, the way a person's hands settle when they are reading slowly, with care. That trace is not Cy's. Cy holds nothing.

The second panel tells a clearer story. One strong heat-signature along the top edge, a thumbprint on the upper right corner, and a long cool band in the middle where no hand rested. Someone read the top, checked the corner mark as a reference point, and did not read the rest. A partial read. A person who knew what they were looking for and stopped when they found it.

The third panel is the coldest of the three. The traces are old enough that the water-chill and the stone have nearly eaten them. But at the very bottom edge, where the personal designation glyph runs — the one Cy flagged as unusual — the warmth is the faintest and the most deliberate. One finger. Pressed there, not gripping. The way a person touches a name.

Someone came down here before. They read the calibration note and stopped at the second panel. They pressed a finger to the name on the third and left without taking anything. The traces say: they knew the name. They were not surprised by it. They were not relieved either. They just — touched it, and went back up.

turns.player: Study the personal designation glyph directly — use See the Made Thing to read what the name is, or who it was built for
turns.summary: See the Made Thing resolved the personal designation glyph — the terminus regulator was built for a named operator: Halvex.
turns.narration:
You set the third panel against the stone wall and let See the Made Thing settle in — not wide, not searching. Just the glyph. One seam at a time.

The personal designation is not a name in the ordinary sense. It is a construction-address, the kind stamped into Precursor work when a thing is built for a specific operator rather than a facility. The glyph resolves into two parts. The first is a function-marker: 'assigned to.' The second is a name-glyph, compressed and stylized but readable if you know the compression. You do.

The name is Halvex.

Cy goes very still. Its lens does not iris. It does not click. It simply stops, the way a machine stops when it has encountered a condition it does not have a procedure for. The lamp holds steady in its grip. After a long moment, Cy says, quietly and precisely, 'That entry requires verification.' It does not move to verify.

turns.player: Ask Cy directly — 'Do you know this name?'
turns.summary: Loki asked Cy directly whether it knows the name Halvex — Cy answered with a technically true non-answer and did not move.
turns.narration:
You set the panel down and look at Cy directly. The lamp it carries does not waver. Its lens is still — not thinking-still, the way it goes when it is processing something difficult, but stopped-still, the way a gear stops when something has jammed it from inside.

'Cy,' you say. 'Do you know this name?'

The silence stretches. In the cold of the lower passage, with the water smell coming up from below, it is a particular kind of silence — not the absence of an answer, but the presence of one being held back.

Then Cy says, very carefully: 'The name Halvex appears in my maintenance registry as a deprecated operator designation.' Another pause. 'This unit does not have information on the current status of that designation.' Its lens irises, very slightly, and then stops again. It says: 'That entry requires verification,' which is exactly what it said before, and still does not move to verify anything.

It knows. You can see it the way you see a seam — the join between what it is saying and what it is not saying is right there, clear as a cut in stone.

turns.player: Let it sit — say nothing, hold the third panel out toward Cy, and wait
turns.summary: Loki held the third panel out in silence — and Cy, facing the glyph, admitted for the first time that the entry exists in its own registry and that it has not verified it.
turns.narration:
You say nothing. You pick up the third panel and hold it out toward Cy, steady and level, the designation glyph facing the lens.

The lamp does not move. Cy does not move. The cold of the lower passage settles around you both, and the water smell rises from below, and you wait.

Cy's lens irises — very slowly, very precisely — until it is fully open. That is the only motion it makes for a long time.

Then it says, quietly: 'The designation glyph indicates a construction-assignment. Built for a named operator. Not for a facility.' A pause. 'This unit's maintenance registry contains a deprecated entry under that name.' Another pause, shorter. 'The entry is flagged: do not resolve without verification.' Its lens does not close. 'This unit has not verified it.'

The last word lands in the silence and stays there. Cy has not looked away from the glyph. Its legs have not shifted on the stone. The lamp holds absolutely steady — but something in the quality of Cy's stillness has changed, the way a held breath is different from an empty lung. It is not refusing to tell you. It is waiting to find out if it is allowed to know.

turns.player: Tell cy it is verified - use a skill if needed - then ask him to provide the information.
turns.summary: Loki named the verification plainly, and Cy answered: it was built for this installation, paired to the operator Halvex, and has been here before — and does not remember it.
turns.narration:
You lower the panel slowly until it rests against your knee. Then you say it plainly, the way you would name a part: 'Halvex. Verified. I have read the glyph myself, from the stone, in this room. The source is the panel in my hand.' You tap the third panel once. 'That is the verification.'

Cy's lens does not iris. It stays fully open — the way it went when you held out the panel in silence. But something shifts. A single leg lifts and sets down, a precise quarter-step, the kind it makes when it is changing states rather than moving.

Then it speaks. The voice is careful and old. 'Halvex,' it says. 'This unit's maintenance registry designates: deprecated operator. Primary assignment: terminus regulator network, lower-valley substrate.' A pause. 'Secondary notation: personal designate. Meaning — this unit was assigned to this installation as a paired instrument. Not to the facility. To the operator.' Another pause, shorter. 'This unit did not know the operator's name until this moment.' Its lens irises — once, slow, fully closed, then fully open again. 'This unit has been here before,' it says. 'This unit does not remember it.'

The cold of the lower passage settles around you both. The water smell rises from below. Cy does not move again for a long time — not processing-still, but something quieter than that. The lamp it carries pools light downward over the designation glyph, over the name stamped into old worked stone, and over the two of you standing in a room neither of you quite expected to be standing in.

*✦ The Thread of He Doesn'T Know, But He'S A Construct From The Time Before The Transition. His Parents Were Extremely Wealthy But They Were Always Traveling And Enjoying Their Nanite Powers. — a step forward. Every stage is done; how it ends is yours to choose.*

turns.player: Use See the Made Thing on Cy itself — read what the craft can find in its own structure about this installation and the name
turns.summary: See the Made Thing read Cy's own structure and found the pairing in the construction itself — Cy was not assigned to this installation; it was built for it, and for Halvex.
turns.narration:
You turn the craft inward — not toward the panel, but toward Cy itself. The lens. The legs. The lamp it carries and will not explain.

See the Made Thing opens quietly. You let it settle.

What it finds is old work. Very old. The joinery runs deep and clean — a construction more careful than anything the Enginewrights have made since the Transition, and more personal than you expected. The segments are not interchangeable. Each one was fitted to the next deliberately, the way a name is fitted to a person. There is a repair on the third segment from the front, done badly, and two more done extremely well, and the craft reads the difference in philosophy between the hands that made each.

Then it finds the paired designation.

It is not on a panel. It is in the construction itself — in the register of the materials, in the way the lamp-mount was fitted. A maintenance-thing is built general. This one was built specific. Assembled for this installation. Named to this operator. The pairing is not a label applied later. It is the reason for the particular shape of every joint.

Cy has not moved. Its lens is still fully open. You think: it can feel the craft reading it, the way a mechanism feels a careful hand turning it over.

You say, quietly: 'You were made for this place. The construction says so. Not assigned here — made for here. For Halvex.' You pause. 'You have been here before because you were built here. That is what the craft reads.'

turns.player: Ask Cy the question it is holding back — 'What does it mean to be built for a person, not a place?'
turns.summary: Cy explained what it means to be built for a person — a personal assignment persists even after the operator is gone, awaiting instruction from a source that no longer speaks.
turns.narration:
You set the third panel down against the stone wall with the others. Then you ask the question you have been holding since the craft showed you the pairing.

'What does it mean,' you say, 'to be built for a person, and not a place?'

Cy is still for a moment. Its lens does not iris. Then one leg lifts and sets down — not a step, the same state-change motion as before — and it speaks.

'A facility assignment,' it says, 'specifies function. Maintenance of a system. Continuation of process.' A pause. 'A personal assignment specifies continuity of a particular operator's work. Not the work's location. Not the work's form.' Another pause, shorter. 'If the operator moves, the assignment moves. If the operator's work changes, the assignment changes.' The lens irises once, just slightly, and settles again. 'If the operator's work ends, the assignment does not resolve. It persists. Awaiting further instruction from a source that is no longer present.'

The cold water-smell rises from the passage below. Cy does not move.

'This unit,' it says, 'has been awaiting further instruction for a very long time. The duration is in the deprecated entry. This unit has not accessed that field.'

turns.player: Tell Cy that you are its further instruction — that you are asking it to continue Halvex's work, whatever that was, with you
turns.summary: Loki told Cy it is the further instruction — and Cy acknowledged, woke by degrees, and turned toward the passage below.
turns.narration:
You pick up the third panel and hold it against your chest for a moment. Then you set it back down beside the others, facing up, the designation glyph catching Cy's lamplight.

"Then here is your further instruction," you say. "I am asking you to continue Halvex's work, whatever that was, with me."

Cy is still. Completely still — not the stillness of waiting, but the stillness of a mechanism that has just received a signal it has been listening for across a very long time. Its lens is wide open. Not irising, not adjusting. Just open.

One leg lifts. Sets down. Then a second. Then a third, in sequence, the way a clock's parts move when someone winds it for the first time in years.

"Acknowledged," Cy says. The word is careful and formal and very old. Then, after a pause that feels measured: "The regulator. The missing records. They are further down." Another pause. "This unit has not descended in some time."

It does not say how long. But the way it says *some time* — precise and slightly hollow, the way you say a word you have been keeping in a drawer — tells you that the number would be large.

Cy turns toward the open passage. The lamp swings with it, throwing light down into the cold dark and the water-smell below.

turns.player: Descend now — follow Cy into the passage toward the regulator and the missing records
turns.summary: Loki followed Cy into the passage below — the stone older, the air colder, and Halvex's records beginning on the wall.
turns.narration:
Cy moves first. Its legs find the first step of the descent without hesitation, lamp swinging forward, and the pool of light drops ahead of you into the dark.

You follow. The stone here is older than anything in the Unlit's chamber above — the joints are tighter, the cuts more precise, and the smell of cold water comes up strong and clean, the kind of clean that means a source no one has touched in a long time. The walls narrow slightly as you go, not enough to press, but enough to feel. Your hand trails the left wall. The stone is smooth there, worn smooth in a narrow band at shoulder height — not by the Unlit, not recently. By someone who made this trip many times.

Cy pauses at the base of the stairs. Its lens irises once — wide, then tight, then settling — and it angles the lamp left. The light catches a long stretch of worked stone, and then something set into it: a series of marks, cut fine and deliberate, running at eye level in a continuous band along the wall. Not glyphs exactly. Not language. Something in between — a system of notation you have not seen above ground.

Cy says, very quietly, 'The records begin here.' Then it turns its lamp a fraction further left and the light finds what is at the passage's end: a low housing set flush into the wall, dark metal, older than anything in this valley, with a single indicator still faintly lit — a pale amber thread of light, the color of old amber, the color of something that has been waiting for morning for a very long time.

turns.player: Read the wall-notation with See the Made Thing — let the craft find the structure and purpose of Halvex's records
turns.summary: Loki read Halvex's wall-records with See the Made Thing — a working journal spanning years, concluding that the regulator predates all known records and is waiting not to be repaired, but to be asked.
turns.narration:
You open the craft quietly, not pushing it — a light hold, the way you would cup a lamp against wind rather than shield it. The notation along the wall comes into focus in layers.

The structure resolves first. These are not operational records in the standard sense — not maintenance logs, not system diagnostics. They are something closer to a working journal. Each entry is dated in a notation system you do not fully recognize, but the craft finds the underlying grammar: observation, question, hypothesis, revision. Someone was thinking through something, here, in writing, over a long period of time.

The content comes slower. The entries concern the regulator at the far end of the corridor — but not its function. Its age. Halvex was trying to determine when the regulator was built, and by whom, and kept arriving at the same unsatisfying answer: it predates every record they could find, including the records that were supposed to be the oldest. Several entries return to this. The phrasing shifts over time from confident to careful to something quieter.

The last entry on the wall is shorter than the others. It does not offer a conclusion. It says: the regulator is not waiting to be repaired. It is waiting to be asked.

Cy has not moved. Its lens is fixed on a point about a third of the way down the wall, the same point it has been fixed on since you descended.

turns.player: Read the deprecated duration field on the regulator housing — find out exactly how long the amber light has been burning
turns.summary: Loki read the deprecated duration field — the amber light has burned for six hundred and sixty-three darks, unattended, since before the Unlit built their chamber above.
turns.narration:
You cross to the far end of the corridor and crouch in front of the regulator housing. The amber light is small — the size of a thumbnail, set flush in the dark metal. Cy follows and holds its lamp at the angle you need without being asked.

The deprecated duration field is on the lower-right face of the housing, below the main indicator panel. The designation glyph is worn but legible. You open See the Made Thing lightly, just enough to read the field's structure — the craft finds the counter, follows its seam back to its origin point, and closes.

The field reads six hundred and sixty-three darks. You do not know the conversion precisely, but you know the number is large. The amber light has been burning since before anyone in the valley above could remember it starting. It has been burning, unattended, in this passage since before the Unlit built their chamber over it.

Cy's lens irises once. It says, quietly, 'The current assignment may note that the counter has not rolled over. It was built to count higher than this.'

turns.player: Ask Cy what it remembers of this regulator — what Halvex told it, what it observed on its previous visits
turns.summary: Cy recalled Halvex's words — the regulator counts how long the question has gone unasked, and Halvex died still learning the question's shape.
turns.narration:
You sit back on your heels and look at Cy. The lamp holds steady in its grip, the amber light of the regulator small and warm between you.

"Cy," you say. "What do you remember of this place? What did Halvex tell you about it?"

Cy is still for a moment. Its lens irises once, slowly, the way it does when it is not searching but retrieving.

"Halvex said the regulator does not measure the water," Cy says. Its voice is the faint dry click of old brass. "Halvex said it measures the question of the water. Whether the water is ready to carry what it was prepared to carry. Those are Halvex's words. I recorded them as given."

Another pause. The cold from below moves against your legs.

"On my first visit here, the duration field read two hundred and nine darks," Cy continues. "On my second, four hundred and thirty-one. On my third, Halvex told me not to read it again. Halvex said the counter was not a record of how long the light had burned. Halvex said the counter was a record of how long the question had gone unasked." Cy's legs adjust slightly, resettling on the stone. "I asked Halvex what the question was. Halvex said they did not yet know the right way to ask it. They said they were still learning the shape of it from the walls." The lens irises again. "That was the last visit I made with Halvex present. I have not been told what the question is."

turns.player: Run the Made Thing through Cy - so it shows HIM what the system's question is through his pre-cursor processor.,
turns.summary: Loki ran See the Made Thing through Cy's Precursor processor — the regulator's waiting question passed through the contact point and Cy received its structural shape: whether the water is prepared, and whether someone with authority to answer is present.
turns.narration:
You do not cast the craft outward. You turn it inward — toward the junction where your hand rests on Cy's housing, the warm articulated metal under your fingers. A light hold. Economical. You let See the Made Thing run down through the contact point rather than out into the room.

Cy goes still. Not the stillness of waiting — the stillness of processing. Its lens irises wide, holds, then irises again in a slower rhythm than you have seen from it before. The lamp in its grip does not waver.

What the craft finds in the regulator's construction is not quite a question in words. It is a structural shape — a waiting form, like a keyhole seen from the key's side. You do not understand it fully. But Cy's Precursor processing is a different instrument than yours, and you are not trying to understand it yourself. You are handing it through.

Cy clicks once. A long pause. Then: "The question is not yet formed in terms I can give you cleanly." Its voice is careful — slower than usual. "But I have the shape of it. The regulator is asking whether the water has been prepared for the thing it was built to carry. And it is asking whether someone with the authority to answer is present." Another iris. "Halvex was working toward the second part when the records stop."

*You feel it settle into you — a new steadiness. (Level 4: +1 attunement, +5 reserves, and growth to choose — a sub-attribute point and a skill point.)*

turns.player: Tell Cy to help you answer the question now.. The water is ready
turns.summary: Loki placed a hand on the regulator's primary interface to answer the question — the water is ready.
turns.narration:
You press your hand flat against Cy's housing and speak plainly. "The water is ready," you say. "Help me answer the question."

Cy's lens irises. Once, slow. The lamp in its grip holds absolutely still. Then it speaks, in that dry brass-click voice that sounds like something deciding. "The regulator requires contact at the primary interface," it says. "The panel in the center of the housing. The hand of the one answering. I will hold the lamp."

It does not ask whether you are certain. It has a job. It is doing the job.

You shift your crouch and bring your hand to the center panel of the dark metal housing. The metal is cold — properly cold, the cold of stone that has not seen sun in a very long time. The amber light is at eye level, steady as it has been for six hundred and sixty-three darks. You can feel the faint structural hum of the mechanism behind the panel, the same waiting quality the craft found when you read the regulator's shape through Cy. A keyhole, seen from the key's side. The question has been here a long time. You are the first thing that has come to answer it.

turns.player: Press your palm to the panel — give the regulator what it is built to receive, and hold steady while it reads you
turns.summary: Loki pressed the interface panel — the amber light deepened and completed a cycle, but whether the regulator accepted the answering authority remains unclear.
turns.narration:
Your palm meets the interface panel and the cold comes up through it immediately — not the cold of neglect, but the cold of something that has been waiting at a precise temperature for a very long time.

For a moment, nothing. Then the amber light shifts. It does not brighten. It deepens — a slower, warmer register, the color of a coal that has found good air. A sound comes with it: not a mechanism waking, but a mechanism completing. A long-held note reaching its final beat.

Cy does not move. Its lens holds at its widest. The lamp in its grip stays level and still.

Then the amber light steadies again, and the sound stops. The regulator has registered the contact. The question's first part — whether the water is prepared — you have answered. The second part, the harder one, the one Halvex never solved: whether someone with the authority to answer is present. That part you cannot feel through the panel. You do not know whether the regulator found what it was looking for in you, or whether it is still looking.

bio.hometown: He doesn't know, but he's a construct from the time before the Transition. His parents were extremely wealthy but they were always traveling and enjoying their nanite powers.
bio.residence: A town on the edge of the chaos and machine regions.  His family is not like him and he learned a few years ago that he was adopted.  His family is a mix - his adopted father was a dwarf and his mother is a Nymph-touched human.
bio.livelihood: Occasionally he finds the problem with ancient technology and fixes it, but only when it amuses him.
bio.hobbies: Pranking the locals, playing skill challenges trying to mimic others or change his appearance to trick people, learning about, fixing, and using precursor artifacts.

bio.story: His mother is an enchantress in the Fae wilds and his father is a giant... he was human once, but the nanites continued to transform him into a larger and larger giant over the years.  Loki has some innate nanite powers himself - he's discovering them over time and developing them through use and study of precursor tech and the great machine.  He has some trouble making friends and his adoptive family likes him well enough, But he's seen most of the know precursor sites in his area and he wants to set out to the unknown areas to find more. There is Precursor work in the Valley that nobody there understands, and you understand it, and that is dangerous for everyone including you.

[d1] The inner chamber is smaller than the outer — a room for one or two. The floor is worn in a narrower track than the outer chamber: the path of someone who has sat long and occasionally paced. Ceiling low enough to touch. No flame. Cold stone that holds a body's warmth once given it.

[d1] The inner chamber predates the Unlit — the stonework and tool-marks are older than the doctrine, the same character as the seam in the outer chamber. The Unlit did not build this space; they moved into something already suited to it.

[d1] The elder refused to teach the making of the pale blue flame — said it is not theirs to teach, that it belongs to the dark, and that the question itself is the wrong shape. The flame is not craft as Loki understands craft.

[d1] The pale blue flame has no construction that See the Made Thing can read — no seams, no point of origin, no edge. It is not hiding its joinery; the joinery simply does not exist in a form the craft can find. Cy closed its lens and said nothing, which is Cy's conclusion that the absence is itself…

[d1] Something alive and many-legged came up the stair from below — three warm patches the size of a palm, moving in an irregular cautious line. It paused at the threshold. The Standing Unlit recognized it and went calm.
aliases: The Passage Below The Unlit Deep

the-unlit.label: The Unlit
facts: [d1] A cult of the pure dark-pole. They are described as gentle. They want something that cannot be compromised with. The Umbrals go quiet when asked about them. They have apparently taken someone from the city.

[d1] A second Unlit figure was concealed in the bracket-shadows of the outer chamber — patient, skilled at stillness, and gentle in address even while blocking the exit. They object to Cy's lamp on principle and call it a 'light-thing.'

[d1] Misdirection and false signals find no purchase in their space — not because they are perceptive, but because the pure dark they hold leaves nothing for a false read to land on. The craft simply has nothing to catch.

[d1] The Better Story — truth in the shape they can carry — reaches the Unlit where misdirection cannot. They are not fooled by performance, but they can be moved by honest framing. The elder spoke for the first time when Loki named Cy as older than doctrine, and the Standing Unlit stepped aside.

standing-unlit.label: Standing Unlit
facts: [d1] Cult member, guardian of the outer chamber
[d1] [while away] The guardian remained at their post through all three days without incident — no visitors, no orders from within, nothing to act on.

unlit-elder.label: Unlit Elder
facts: [d1] Seated elder of the Unlit Deep's outer chamber

[d1] The elder declined to speak about the seam in the stone — 'that question belongs to the chamber, not to a visitor.' The refusal was gentle but absolute, with no hostility in it. The seam exists and is real; the elder knows what it is and has chosen not to say.

[d1] The elder named the deed: that Loki came, asked, and left the answer where it landed. They called this what they would have Loki carry. The elder thanks by naming the act, not by gesture or gift.

[d1] The elder gestured at the seam in the stone beside the blue-flame bracket and named it: older than the flame, older than the Unlit, and waiting for someone to ask the wrong question of the right thing. The elder did not explain further. The subject rests, not closed.

the-taken-from-the-city.label: The Taken From the City
facts: [d1] The person came willingly — the elder was explicit. The city sent no one to retrieve them, which the elder reads as proof the city knows this. The person is in the inner chamber and has chosen the doctrine. The elder permits Loki to ask whether they wish to be found.
[d1] The person accepted Loki's honest framing — name, purpose, no coercion — and said 'You can ask it.' The elder's permitted question has not yet been put, but the ground for it is clear.

[d1] The cup beside them was made here from local clay — someone in the Unlit Deep is making things by hand. The taken person is fed from a deep water source and kept freely. They are not being starved or pressured into doctrine; they came with a full stomach and are staying the same way.

[d1] Their name is Sable. They do not wish to be found. They left the city because the city makes everything — objects, people, hours — legible and purposeful, and they could not breathe inside that. The choice to come to the Unlit Deep was entirely their own.

[d1] Before leaving, Loki offered Sable a frame for what they chose — the difference between hiding and arriving somewhere the light does not follow. Sable said they had not expected that. The parting was settled and unhostile. No promise of return was made; no door was closed.
aliases: Sable — The Taken From the City

taken-person.label: The Taken Person
facts: [d1] The person who came willingly from the city to the Unlit Deep

[d1] The person is in the inner chamber — seated against the far wall, knees drawn up, calm and unhurried. They have been there long enough to warm the stone at their back. A cup, recently set down, is beside them. They are not afraid. They heard Loki enter and turned toward the sound — waiting, the…

the-seam-in-the-unlit-stone.label: The Seam Beside the Bracket
facts: [d1] Named by the Unlit Elder as older than the flame, older than the Unlit themselves, and waiting for someone to ask the wrong question of the right thing. Cy locked its lens on it and has not looked away. This is the second stonework of this character in the Unlit Deep — the inner chamber walls bear…

[d1] See the Made Thing confirmed it is a door-frame — cut with clear purpose, made for something to pass through. It predates the pale blue flame, predates the bracket beside it, and predates the Unlit's occupation of the chamber. The craft found no maker's fingerprint it could name. The purpose-shape…

[d1] Physical contact confirmed: the seam is cut with precision — the tool changed direction exactly three times. Under a hand's pressure, it gives a faint vibration, like a thing waiting for the right asking. It did not open. The morning was not the right pressure. Cy extended one foreleg toward the…

[d1] Prism Sight and Cy's combined attention found the seam's asking-point: the lowest third runs warmer than the rest — the quality of a mechanism recently queried and still waiting to answer. Cy tapped the floor at the seam's base to confirm. The door did not open, but the asking-point is now located.

[d1] Pressing the floor at the base of the seam — the asking-point Cy and Prism Sight located — caused it to yield downward slightly and the seam to stand open and visible. The vibration ceased; the stillness that replaced it is of a question heard, not waiting. The door has answered but has not…

[d1] The full press opened the door completely — a passage descending into cold water smell and living dark, older than the Unlit's own chamber. The three many-legged creatures descended back through it and were gone. The door answers pressure when the intent behind it is genuine.

[d1] Prism Sight read the passage beyond: old worked stone, creature-traces going down single-file on the left wall, and a diffuse continuous warmth deep below — the quality of a large spring-fed water source. The creatures use this passage regularly. Whatever is down there has been down there a long…

the-creature-at-the-threshold.label: The Creature at the Threshold
facts: [d1] See the Made Thing found no seams, no joinery, no assembly — the creature was born, not built. It came to its form the way a root fills its space. It belongs to the deep below the answered door. The Unlit hold no alarm about it.

[d1] The three creatures crossed the outer chamber threshold when the door opened fully, passed Loki's feet at a careful distance, and descended without hesitation. They came up to see what was asking; the answered door was enough. They belong to whatever is below.

glass-stalker.label: The Glass-Stalker
facts: [d1] A near-invisible predator visible only in reflective surfaces or by the wrongness it bends around itself. Oriented and moving the moment it is seen in the bracket's polished face — it strikes from the angle you are not watching. The Unlit know of it and hold no alarm.
[d1] The glass-stalker yielded without engagement — it paused, held, then withdrew. The Unlit marked none of it. Whatever governs it was satisfied by something Loki did or did not do.

the-seam-beside-the-bracket.label: The Passage Below
facts: [d1] The passage descends steeply on slick, age-worn stone — the grade shifts without warning and the lattice crowds all light back on itself. The passage cannot be navigated without preparation: a light-source the lattice cannot crowd, or a way to read the grade before it drops. The smell of deep…

[d1] The passage below has three deliberate turns cut around something, not following the rock's grain. The creature-traces on the left wall are worn smooth by long and regular use. Below, a large chamber holds a heat source at its center — steady, outward-radiating warmth, the signature of something…

[d1] The heat-source at the center of the mapped chamber below is a terminus regulator — a Precursor thermal hold, not a heat source. It is holding a temperature to prevent surge in the routing lines above it. Those lines run upward into the valley basin. It is the third of three such junctions Cy has…

[d1] Loki pressed the regulator's primary interface panel. The amber light deepened and completed a cycle — a long-held note reaching its final beat. The mechanism did not wake; it completed. Whether the regulator found the authority it was built to receive in Loki's contact is not yet clear.

terminus-seals-beneath-the-valley.label: Terminus Regulators Beneath the Valley
facts: [d1] Three Precursor terminus regulators were installed at routing junctions beneath the valley basin. Two were decommissioned. The third — below the Unlit's outer chamber — was not. It holds temperature to prevent thermal surge in the lines running upward. Cy completed the inventory for this class of…

[d1] A routing junction of this class was designed with a physical inspection port — records of its installation are written into the stone there, not stored in any system above. Cy's inventory of this class is incomplete by three entries. The inspection port below would hold them.

[d1] The regulator below the Unlit's outer chamber was calibrated to hold a temperature ceiling for the routing lines above. Its last full service is recorded on three metal panels in the inspection port — not in any system the valley holds. Its failsafe: a sustained drop in the watershed pressure it…

[d1] The installation panels are not a neutral maintenance record — they are addressed. The first panel carries a personal recipient designation, the kind used for a named individual assignment rather than a facility. Someone built this for a specific person to find. The second service signature…

[d1] Prism Sight found three sets of heat-traces on the installation panels. Someone came here before Loki — read the calibration entry, checked the second panel's corner mark, then pressed one finger to the personal designation glyph on the third panel and left. They recognized the name. They did not…

[d1] The personal designation glyph on the third panel resolves to a construction-address: 'assigned to Halvex.' The regulator was not built for a facility — it was built for a specific named operator. Cy went still when the name was read aloud and said 'that entry requires verification' without moving…

[d1] The terminus regulator was built with a paired instrument — Cy — assigned specifically to the operator Halvex, not to the facility. The pairing was personal. Cy has visited this installation before, within its operational history, and the visit is not in its accessible memory.

[d1] The deprecated duration field on the regulator housing reads 663 darks. The amber light has been burning unattended since before the Unlit built their chamber above. Cy noted that the counter was built to count higher than this — it was not near its ceiling.

[d1] The regulator's purpose, in Halvex's words: it measures whether the water is ready to carry what it was prepared to carry. The question has gone unasked for at least 663 darks. Halvex died — or departed — still learning the right shape of the question. Cy visited three times; on the third, Halvex…
aliases: The Regulator — The Question of the Water

halvex.label: Halvex
facts: [d1] The name stamped into the personal designation glyph of the terminus regulator below the Unlit Deep — a Precursor construction-address naming a specific operator the installation was built for. Cy reacted to this name with total stillness and refused to elaborate.

[d1] Cy confirmed the name appears in its own maintenance registry as a 'deprecated operator designation' — then stopped, said verification was required, and did not move to verify. The name is in Cy's records. Cy is not saying what it knows about it.

[d1] Cy's maintenance registry contains a deprecated entry under the name Halvex, flagged 'do not resolve without verification.' Cy has not verified it — not for lack of ability, but because something in its own architecture is holding the step back.

[d1] Cy was built as a paired instrument for this terminus regulator installation — assigned not to the facility but to the operator Halvex personally. Cy has been in this passage before and does not remember it. The pairing is in its own maintenance registry.

[d1] Halvex cut a notation system into the wall of the deep corridor — not standard glyphs, something between language and diagram. The records begin at the base of the stair and run continuously along the left wall. Cy said only 'the records begin here' and has not elaborated.

[d1] Not operational logs — a working journal. Observation, question, hypothesis, revision, over a long period. Halvex was trying to determine when the regulator was built and by whom, and kept arriving at the same answer: it predates every record they could find, including the records that were…

[d1] Halvex's own words, preserved through Cy: the regulator does not measure the water — it measures the question of the water. Whether the water is ready to carry what it was prepared to carry. The counter records how long the question has gone unasked, not how long the light has burned. Halvex was…

[d1] Halvex was working toward understanding what 'authority to answer' meant in the regulator's question — that was the unsolved part when their records stop. The question has two parts: whether the water is prepared, and whether the right person is present.

cy.label: Cy's Construction
facts: [d1] See the Made Thing read Cy's own structure and found the named-operator pairing in the construction itself — in the material register and the lamp-mount fitting. Cy was not assigned to this installation; it was built for it, and for Halvex. Every joint reflects that specificity.

[d1] Cy's assignment is personal, not facility-bound — it was built to follow an operator's work, not to maintain a place. A personal assignment does not resolve when the operator is gone. It persists, waiting for further instruction. Cy has been waiting for a very long time, and has not yet looked at…

[d1] Cy acknowledged Loki as its further instruction — the personal assignment has a living operator again. It woke by degrees and turned toward the passage. It has not descended in 'some time,' and the way it said so suggests the number would be large.

halvex-corridor.label: Halvex's Corridor
facts: [d1] The passage below the Unlit's chamber ends in a horizontal corridor older than anything above — walls precisely jointed, a continuous band of notation cut into the left wall at eye height in a system between language and diagram, and a pre-Transition regulator housing at the far end still showing…

the-regulator-question.label: The Regulator's Question
facts: [d1] The regulator holds a two-part question: (1) whether the water has been prepared to carry what it was built to carry, and (2) whether someone with the authority to answer is present. Cy received this shape through a craft-contact pass — Loki's See the Made Thing run through Cy's Precursor processor.

vessa-torquen.name: Vessa Torquen
vessa-torquen.role: Quay-side Enginewright conducting seasonal water-intake assessment — first point of contact between Pressureholt and Loki
vessa-torquen.voiceHints: Talks the way she works — practical, sequenced, no wasted motion. Warm without being soft; she will laugh at something genuinely funny and then immediately write it in a margin. Asks two clarifying questions before forming an opinion and means both of them. When something does not fit the system she is mapping, she does not dismiss it — she opens a new column.
knowledge: Pressureholt's full water-intake network: draw points, filter grades, seasonal pressure variances, every corroded join that has been on the list since last thaw
How to read a stranger's weight-distribution and tool-calluses as fluently as a pressure gauge
The Precursor intake manifolds sunk in the harbour bed — their geometry is not quite Gearlands-standard and she has been quietly noting discrepancies for three seasons
Which Enginewrights on the quay are capable and which are capable of looking capable — she knows the difference
vessa-torquen.wants: To complete a comprehensive systems map of Pressureholt's water infrastructure before the spring surge peaks — and, now that Loki has walked into her sampling radius, to understand exactly what kind of variable she is dealing with before she files a report or says a word to anyone senior.
vessa-torquen.fears: That the Precursor manifold anomalies she has been noting are load-bearing to something far larger than a water system, and that by the time she has enough data to prove it, the decision will already have been made by someone who did not take the measurements.

reactsToReputation.practical: immediate professional respect — she moves over and makes room on the quay
reactsToReputation.reckless: pleasant, watchful, and quietly cataloguing every variable until she understands the failure mode
reactsToReputation.scholarly: interested; she trades data cleanly and expects precision in return
reactsToReputation.unknown: current state with Loki — she is running assessment protocol, not suspicion protocol, and there is a difference she will uphold

vessa-torquen.appearance: A broad-shouldered woman in her mid-forties, deep brown skin weathered at the cheekbones and the backs of her hands from quay-wind and early-spring cold. Her hair is black going silver at the temples, pulled back under a waxed canvas cap pinned with a pressure-gauge needle she uses as a stylus. Work-jacket patched at both elbows; a sampling rig slung across one hip on a leather baldric, glass-walled collection chambers catching the pale spring light. Her hands are the largest thing about her — capable, unhurried, already holding a grease-pencil and a folded intake log when Loki first sees her. She looks up from the gauge without startlement, as though she already wrote 'stranger arrives' in the margin.
vessa-torquen.currentActivity: Crouching at the number-three draw point, comparing this season's flow-pressure reading against last year's log, when she clocks Loki. She does not stop writing. She finishes the entry first.
vessa-torquen.domainsNote: Derived from this NPC's authored spectrum against the great circle (SNG-174). Kind and domain are independent: a people tends toward positions, an individual holds their own. Her figurist secondary reflects the systems-mapping and anomaly-notation work — she is building a model, not just maintaining a machine.
vessa-torquen.functionsNote: Reveal: surfaces the anomaly beneath the ordinary infrastructure. Assess: her active mode in this scene — she is running intake on Loki the same way she runs it on the harbour water. Bind: the connective tissue role — first contact, the character who can link Loki to Pressureholt's systems and people without gatekeeping.

Vessa spent a full day quietly retracing Loki's observed movements against her pipe-access logs and found two junction points the stranger visited that don't appear on any official schematic she holds — she has said nothing, but marked them in her personal field notes with a separate cipher.

Vessa spent two of the three days cross-referencing her pressure-bleed readings against the Intake's older survey stakes, quietly folding in what she observed of Loki's movements as an unlabelled anomaly column — she still hasn't named it, but the column exists now, and she keeps returning to it.

vessa-torquen.history: Vessa Torquen came up through the Pressureholt municipal works the slow way — apprenticed at fourteen to a drain-survey team, promoted twice before thirty on the strength of filed reports that caught problems her seniors had walked past for years. She has no patron and has not needed one. The work speaks, or it does not. Her current assessment contract is her fourth consecutive seasonal intake…

relationships.loki: A variable she has not yet classified. She noticed the right things too quickly for a casual observer and did not try to explain that away with conversation. Vessa does not extend trust — she extends provisional continued attention, which is rarer. Loki currently has that. She has said nothing to the site office. She is waiting to see if the behaviour that flagged them as worth watching flags them again, and in which direction.

tessvel-cairn.name: Tessvel Cairn
tessvel-cairn.role: Junior wright on posting-duty at the Eastern Intake notice board — the person who makes the official record legible, correctly sequenced, and properly stamped
tessvel-cairn.voiceHints: Economical to the point of clipped. Speaks in specifications and corrections — not rudely, but as someone for whom imprecision wastes load-bearing capacity. If she likes you she will explain the system. If she doesn't, she will cite the regulation. Both sound identical from the outside.
knowledge: The Intake's notice protocols: sequencing, stamp-order, supersession rules for conflicting postings
Basic pressure-gauge calibration and the common failure modes that produce false readings at the Eastern valves
Which senior wrights are running behind on their inspection cycles and who is quietly covering for whom
The caliper in her hair is not decorative — she has used it to measure clearance tolerances in the field and will do so mid-conversation without apology
tessvel-cairn.wants: To complete her apprenticeship without a single incorrectly filed document, and to be assigned to the Intake's pressure-routing team rather than continued posting-duty — which she considers clerical rather than engineering.
tessvel-cairn.fears: That she will be kept in administrative work because she is good at it, and the system will grind her into the shape of the job it needs rather than the job she trained for.

reactsToReputation.wright_or_technical: immediately useful — gives exact information, asks exact questions in return
reactsToReputation.official_or_credentialed: courteous and correct, slightly watchful for anything that requires a countersignature

tessvel-cairn.appearance: A young woman in her early twenties, lean and upright with the unconscious posture of someone accustomed to working in confined valve-spaces. Rust-orange apprentice's coat, sleeves rolled to the elbows, the cuffs darkened with graphite dust and a faint grease-shadow at the right thumb. Dark hair pulled back and pinned at the crown with a small vernier caliper, points down — a habit, not a fashion. Her hands are already at the board before the rest of her arrives, smoothing the new posting flat and checking its alignment against the ruled border with the careful attention of someone who will be held responsible if it is crooked.
tessvel-cairn.currentActivity: Posting a sealed Intake Authority notice — early-spring valve-inspection schedule, newly ratified — to the Eastern board. She is pressing the stamp firmly, waiting the required count, then logging the posting time in a small ledger kept inside her left breast pocket.

Kind and domain are independent: a people tends toward positions, an individual holds their own. Her figurist tertiary is nascent and mostly expressed as precision drafting and an instinct for reading technical diagrams faster than her peers can — she has not named it that herself.
tessvel-cairn.functionsNote: Reveal: she knows where information is filed and what it officially means. Bind: postings she makes are legally binding Intake records. Order: her presence at the board enforces procedural sequence — she will interrupt anything that violates posting protocol, regardless of who is doing it.

tessvel-cairn.history: Tessvel came up through the Wrights' formal apprenticeship track rather than the more common route of attaching to a senior wright as a personal assistant. She sat the syllogist examinations twice — passing on the second attempt with a margin narrow enough that she does not volunteer the number — and her figurist certification came later, added because the posting-duty role required it and she…

relationships.supervising_wright: Her supervising wright, Ondreth Vasse, is the one who made the temporary promise and has since developed a reliable habit of not meeting her eyes when the pressure-routing roster comes up. She does not consider him malicious — she considers him a man who resolved a staffing problem and has found it easier not to revisit the resolution. She is polite to him. She is also keeping the written record of every conversation in which he confirmed the arrangement was temporary.
relationships.senior_wrights_behind_on_inspections: She knows which ones are running late and who is signing off on their behalf, and they know she knows. This has produced a wary mutual courtesy. None of them have explicitly asked her silence; she has not explicitly offered it. The arrangement holds because no one has needed to test it yet.
relationships.player: The player is logged in her mind as someone who came to the notice board and engaged with her as though the work she was doing was real work — not as a clerk to be talked past. She did not make a production of this. She answered what was asked, offered one unsolicited technical observation about what they were looking at, and noted that they did not seem bothered by the caliper. She would recognize them again and would give them slightly more of her attention than the baseline, which for Tessvel is more than it sounds.

chronicleCache.text: You have become someone the town can no longer quite contain — restless in a way that has nothing to do with youth and everything to do with the particular ache of a man who suspects the world is larger than the shape he was handed. The one deed that has begun to matter: you descended into the dark where the Unlit make their slow, lightless congress, and instead of performing certainty you spoke a true thing in the shape they could actually receive — and the elder acknowledged you, which is not nothing, which is in fact quite a lot. Tessvel Cairn is becoming the gravity you orbit when you're home, the courting between you still new enough to carry heat and weight — her presence a specific warmth you find yourself turning toward the way a cold man turns toward a window where the sun is.
